Final review complete. The only change is in src/dotenv/main.py, set_key's quoted branch (lines 184-187): backslashes are escaped before apostrophes via `value_to_set.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")`. This aligns the writer with the parser's single-quote escape set (`\\`, `\'`), so literal backslashes — consecutive ones and those adjacent to apostrophes — round-trip exactly through dotenv_values(interpolate=False). quote_mode selection and export handling are untouched, preserving all other public behavior. No tests, docs, other modules, or dependencies were modified.

Remaining limitations: the fix targets single-quoted output only (the mode set_key uses for 'always'/'auto'); quote_mode='never' still writes raw values by design, so values containing newlines or leading/trailing spaces are not round-trippable in that mode — this is pre-existing intended behavior, not part of the reported bug.
